title: Configuring the Development Environment knowledge check

options: This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Terminal and notebook workflows”, what should a learner verify?
options: Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
confirm `sys.executable`, `torch.__version__`, and whether the intended device is available in the same environment.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
questions.answer_key: confirm `sys.executable`, `torch.__version__`, and whether the intended device is available in the same environment.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: confirm `sys.executable`, `torch.__version__`, and whether the intended device is available in the same environment.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Project directory structure”?
options: Do not copy one CUDA/ROCm command for every machine; match the build to the supported hardware and Python version.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
questions.answer_key: Do not copy one CUDA/ROCm command for every machine; match the build to the supported hardware and Python version.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not copy one CUDA/ROCm command for every machine; match the build to the supported hardware and Python version.
